accepted.evidence: Turner 2333 directly cites European Romani opre 'on, over' under *uppari. The source prints Zargari opro [ophro] 'up; above' in §2.3.3 (p. 127), opro 'above' as an adverb (§3.20.1.3, p. 143) and as an adposition (§3.20.2.1, p. 144). The source's optional aspiration is preserved; the two installed opro records cover these attestations. Original PDF, glyph-decoded source audit and imported key checked; no transcription or identity change.

Turner 2333 explicitly cites European Romani opral 'from above', represented by its compiled inferred -l- extension 2333-2. The source prints Zargari opr-āl 'from above' and identifies -āl as the local ablative place suffix (p. 132 §3.1.15). This is directly parallel to Turner's Romani form, while the source's -āl spelling is retained. Original PDF, glyph-decoded source audit and imported key checked; no transcription or identity change.

Turner 14382 explicitly derives European Romani kat 'shears, scissors' from *kārti- rather than karttrī-; 14382 redirects to the substantive *kārti- article 3069. The source prints Zargari kāt/qāt 'scissors' when describing /k/~/q/ free variation before back vowels (§2.3.16, p. 128); the installed kāt is the attested form. Original PDF, glyph-decoded source audit and imported key checked; no transcription or identity change.

Turner 6628 lists European Romani drak(h) 'grape' and Persian Romani dérak under drā́kṣā-. The source prints Zargari de.rāk 'grape' with explicit Early Romani drakh comparison in its syllable-structure examples (§2.4.1, p. 129). The source's initial vowel and local syllabification are retained. Original PDF, glyph-decoded source audit and imported key checked; no transcription or identity change.

Turner 10104 explicitly cites European Romani másek 'month' under mā́sa. The source prints Zargari masik 'month' as a consonant-final noun in §3.1.8 (p. 131); its i/e vowel difference remains source-specific. Original PDF, glyph-decoded source audit and imported key checked; no transcription or identity change.

Turner 988 lists European Romani amaro 'ours' under an -ra-/-kāra- extension of asmā́ka, represented by compiled node 988-2. The source prints Zargari āmāros 'ours' (oblique) and āmārostār 'from ours; with ours' together in its possessive paradigm (p. 135 §3.3.3.1). Source case suffixes are retained; both forms have the same inherited possessive stem. Original PDF, glyph-decoded source audit and imported key checked; no transcription or identity change.
